title: Core revision supersession, epochs and carry binding
description:
Objective: land the pure core half of the graph supersession engine - immutable new revisions, graph epochs, the explicit safe carry binding, and the atomic activation decision - AND make `graph.supersede` a real transition instead of a declared refusal. Slice 1 of 2 from task-dddfaf83f9c644099b5b263e485c58c7, split by architect-d46fcb95 on human direction 2026-08-09 because the whole task needs 13 distinct files against a 10-file hard cap.

*** THE MEASUREMENT THAT DEFINES THIS SLICE. `graph.supersede` is DECLARED BUT DELIBERATELY UNIMPLEMENTED today. packages/core/src/planning/graph-revision-reducer.ts:59 lists it in GRAPH_REVISION_COMMAND_KINDS; :68 gives it an EMPTY admitted-from list in GRAPH_REVISION_TRANSITIONS; :170 routes it to `illegal(state, command.kind)` unconditionally. Separately :196 already refuses every further command once a revision is SUPERSEDED, via supersededAuthority() in graph-revision-results.ts:42. So the vocabulary and the fail-closed guard exist; the transition itself does not. `GraphRevisionSupersedeCommand` exists at graph-revision-contract.ts:77 but carries only a GraphRevisionRefusalWitness - it has no successor/epoch binding, which is exactly what a real supersede needs. ***

Human decision 2026-08-09: this slice owns that transition. Without it the engine would compute dispositions nothing applies, and per global rail Clause 1 a pure package with no consumer edge cannot complete.

MEASURED PRESENT, so nothing here needs a prerequisite:
- packages/core/src/policy/approval-invalidation.ts (task "Policy approval core", DONE) - the carry-invalidation substrate for DoD 3.
- @moe/contracts already ships the vocabulary: SUPERSESSION_CONSEQUENCE_CHANGED, SUPERSEDED_AUTHORITY and REVISION_REBOUND in runtime-error-registry.ts:14; `graph.supersede` in runtime-vocabulary.ts:94; APPROVAL_VALIDITY carries CURRENT/INVALIDATED/SUPERSEDED and GRAPH_REVISION carries SUPERSEDED. Do NOT mint a parallel vocabulary - compose these.
- packages/core/src/planning/graph-revision-{contract,reducer,validation,results}.ts, the lifecycle this slice extends.

MEASURED ABSENT: packages/core/src/supersession/ does not exist.

Deliverable: packages/core/src/supersession/supersession-engine.ts (+ .js bridge) holding the epoch/carry/disposition-kind vocabulary and the pure decision, its focused test, the real `graph.supersede` transition across graph-revision-{contract,reducer,validation}.ts, the updated graph-revision-reducer.test.ts, and curated publication from packages/core/src/index.ts.

NOT in scope: attempt/effect/resource/budget disposition wiring (slice 2), rewriting history, implicit approval carry, daemon persistence, UI.

Owned paths: packages/core/src/supersession/**, packages/core/src/planning/graph-revision-contract.ts, graph-revision-reducer.ts, graph-revision-validation.ts, graph-revision-reducer.test.ts, packages/core/src/index.ts.

Consumers (Clause 1): slice 2 task, and packages/scheduler/src/admission/admission-wait.ts:10 already defers to this by name - "supersession carry of wait/blocker projections -> graph supersession engine".

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test
definitionOfDone: `graph.supersede` is a real transition: GRAPH_REVISION_TRANSITIONS admits it from the exact lifecycles a supersede may act on instead of an empty list, the reducer routes it to a handler instead of `illegal`, and the command carries an explicit successor/epoch binding rather than only a refusal witness.

Old and new revisions never hold overlapping authority outside an explicit safe carry binding: a superseded revision still refuses every further command through the existing supersededAuthority() guard, and the successor's authority is bound by hash to the predecessor it replaced.

Graph epochs are monotonic and a stale epoch cannot mutate current state; a changed or UNKNOWN authority or input fact invalidates carry rather than silently carrying it, composing packages/core/src/policy/approval-invalidation.ts rather than reimplementing invalidation.

Every refusal pins an existing @moe/contracts code - SUPERSESSION_CONSEQUENCE_CHANGED, SUPERSEDED_AUTHORITY or REVISION_REBOUND - and the refusing layer; no parallel vocabulary is minted, and a generated sweep asserts a non-zero case count.

graph-revision-reducer.test.ts is updated deliberately: the assertion that graph.supersede is illegal is replaced by assertions of the new transition, and every OTHER pre-existing assertion in that file passes unchanged; a mutation drill proves each new guard is reddenable.

The supersession surface is published from the core root by a curated named block, and fresh pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test exits 0 with every production file at or below 250 physical lines.
taskRails: This slice changes a landed, QA-passed reducer. graph-revision-reducer.test.ts (222 lines) pins today's behaviour including that graph.supersede is illegal. Update ONLY the assertions that the new transition genuinely invalidates; if any other assertion needs touching, that is a behaviour regression, not a test to adjust.
Compose the @moe/contracts supersession vocabulary and core's approval-invalidation; do not mint a second set of codes or reimplement invalidation inside this module or inside a test helper.
A dependency, readiness or authority claim without verifiable evidence is UNKNOWN or refused; an UNKNOWN fact invalidates carry and never upgrades to a safe carry.
Tests assert the exact stable reason code and the refusing layer, and any generated sweep asserts it produced a non-zero number of cases.
Target <=250 physical lines per production source, split before 400; this cap is per file, not per task.
